paras.text: Lipids have three major subclasses: simple lipids, compound lipids and derived lipids.

paras.text: The monomer that makes up a nucleic acid is called a nucleotide.
paras.urdu: نیوکلک ایسڈ بنانے والے مونومر کو نیوکلیوٹائیڈ کہتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: هغه مونومر چې نیوکلیک اسید جوړوي نیوکلیوټایډ بلل کېږي.

paras.text: Nucleotide has three parts: an inorganic phosphate group, a five-carbon monosaccharide sugar, and a nitrogen containing structure known as a nitrogenous base.
paras.urdu: نیوکلیوٹائیڈ کے تین حصے ہیں: ایک غیر نامیاتی فاسفیٹ گروپ، ایک پانچ کاربن والی مونوسیکرائیڈ شکر، اور نائٹروجن رکھنے والی ساخت جسے نائٹروجنی اساس کہتے ہیں۔

sections.theory:
The substances, which decrease the activity of an enzyme, known as enzyme inhibitor and this process is known as enzyme inhibition.

Lipids have three major subclasses: simple lipids, compound lipids and derived lipids.

The monomer that makes up a nucleic acid is called a nucleotide.

Nucleotide has three parts: an inorganic phosphate group, a five-carbon monosaccharide sugar, and a nitrogen containing structure known as a nitrogenous base.

DNA contains genetic information in the form of codes.

Minerals essential for life are the inorganic nutrients.

Iron is a part of haemoglobin, a carrier of oxygen in the body.

Calcium is the main constituent of bones and teeth.

Living organism cannot synthesized the essential minerals.

Exercise

Q I. Choose the correct one from the given options.

1. The optimum pH of pepsin is around

a. 3.0   b. 3.5   c. 2.0   d. 2.5

2. The most abundant carbohydrate found in nature is

a. cellulose   b. glycogen   c. pectin   d. chitin

3. The glycosidic linkage is present between the molecules of

a. glucose   b. glycine   c. fatty acid   d. none of these

4. Steroid belong to family of

a. carbohydrates   b. proteins   c. lipids   d. enzymes

5. Protein present in haemoglobin has the structure known as

a. primary structure.   b. secondary structure.   c. tertiary structure.   d. quaternary structure.

6. Which carbohydrate does not conform the general formula Cₙ(H₂O)ₙ?

a. Deoxyribose   b. Ribose   c. Glucose   d. Fructose

7. Ethanol is produced from starch by the process of

a. hydrolysis   b. hydrogenation   c. decomposition   d. fermentation

8. Human are unable to digest

a. glucose   b. cellulose   c. starch   d. denatured protein

9. Which one of the following term is not related to term aldohexose?

a. Aldehyde   b. Ketone   c. Six   d. Sugar

10. Slow healing of wounds is due the deficiency of

a. Ca   b. P   c. Zn   d. Fe

11. RNA is primarily seen in

a. nucleus   b. cytoplasm   c. cell wall   d. cell membrane

12. In which of following disaccharides both the basic structural units are the same?

a. Maltose   b. Lactose   c. Sucrose   d. All of these

13. In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor

a. competes with enzyme.   b. irreversibly binds with the enzyme.   c. binds with substrate.   d. competes with substrate.

14. In DNA, adenine forms a complementary pair with which other nitrogen base?

a. Uracil   b. Cytosine   c. Thymine   d. Guanine

15. Proteins are polymers of

a. glucose   b. disulphide bridges   c. amino acids   d. peptide bonds

sections.content:
The substances, which decrease the activity of an enzyme, known as enzyme inhibitor and this process is known as enzyme inhibition.

Lipids have three major subclasses: simple lipids, compound lipids and derived lipids.

The monomer that makes up a nucleic acid is called a nucleotide.

Nucleotide has three parts: an inorganic phosphate group, a five-carbon monosaccharide sugar, and a nitrogen containing structure known as a nitrogenous base.

DNA contains genetic information in the form of codes.

Minerals essential for life are the inorganic nutrients.

Iron is a part of haemoglobin, a carrier of oxygen in the body.

Calcium is the main constituent of bones and teeth.

Living organism cannot synthesized the essential minerals.

Exercise

Q I. Choose the correct one from the given options.

1. The optimum pH of pepsin is around

a. 3.0 b. 3.5 c. 2.0 d. 2.5

2. The most abundant carbohydrate found in nature is

a. cellulose b. glycogen c. pectin d. chitin

3. The glycosidic linkage is present between the molecules of

a. glucose b. glycine c. fatty acid d. none of these

4. Steroid belong to family of

a. carbohydrates b. proteins c. lipids d. enzymes

5. Protein present in haemoglobin has the structure known as

a. primary structure. b. secondary structure. c. tertiary structure. d. quaternary structure.

6. Which carbohydrate does not conform the general formula Cₙ(H₂O)ₙ?

a. Deoxyribose b. Ribose c. Glucose d. Fructose

7. Ethanol is produced from starch by the process of

a. hydrolysis b. hydrogenation c. decomposition d. fermentation

8. Human are unable to digest

a. glucose b. cellulose c. starch d. denatured protein

9. Which one of the following term is not related to term aldohexose?

a. Aldehyde b. Ketone c. Six d. Sugar

10. Slow healing of wounds is due the deficiency of

a. Ca b. P c. Zn d. Fe

11. RNA is primarily seen in

a. nucleus b. cytoplasm c. cell wall d. cell membrane

12. In which of following disaccharides both the basic structural units are the same?

a. Maltose b. Lactose c. Sucrose d. All of these

13. In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor

a. competes with enzyme. b. irreversibly binds with the enzyme. c. binds with substrate. d. competes with substrate.

14. In DNA, adenine forms a complementary pair with which other nitrogen base?

a. Uracil b. Cytosine c. Thymine d. Guanine

15. Proteins are polymers of

a. glucose b. disulphide bridges c. amino acids d. peptide bonds

Take 250cm3 milk in a beaker. Gently warm the milk (not boil), add small amount of lemon juice or vinegar (acetic acid) in it and observe it. Report your observation by answering the following questions.

6. Name some products in which it is used.
